summary: Khuraym bin Faatik tells Umar how a Jinn called him to Islaam and guided him to Madinah, where Umar accepted Uthmaan's testimony to a hadith Khuraym had quoted.
Khuraym bin Faatik recites the Jinn's verses of guidance again, and Ibn Abbaas later tells Umar the story.
notes: Two reports: Khuraym's couplets, then a separate narration of Umar asking Ibn Abbaas for a story.

summary: Umar questions the former fortune-teller Sawaad bin Qaarib, who relates how his Jinn told him of a Nabi from Luway bin Ghaalib, and how he came to the Prophet and accepted Islaam.
notes: Several reports joined: Abdullaah bin Umar, Muhammad bin Ka'b Qurazi, and a Baraa variant. The Umar account at the end is cut off mid-sentence. 'Baraa' is not given a patronymic.

summary: Abbaas bin Mirdaas hears a voice from his idol Dimaad announcing the Prophet's coming, destroys the idol, and with his tribe goes to the Prophet and accepts Islaam.
notes: Main account followed by an 'Another narration' variant of the same incident.

summary: Jaabir and Ali bin Husayn report that a Jinn serving a woman in Madinah brought news of the Prophet's coming and his prohibition of adultery.
notes: Two reports: Jaabir (woman unnamed) and Ali bin Husayn (names her Faatima). Not matched to the Companion Faatima; sahabi status unsure.

summary: Uthmaan recounts that a fortune-teller in Shaam said his Jinn could not enter because Ahmed had appeared, and that when he returned to Makkah the Prophet had already announced his Nabuwwaat.
Mujaahid reports an old man's account of hearing a voice from a cow's belly call people to say that there is none worthy of worship but Allaah, during the Period of Ignorance.

Ibn Abbaas reports how a Shaytaan named Mis'ar stirred the Quraysh against the Muslims through an idol, and how a Jinn named Samhaj, whom the Prophet named Abdullaah after he believed, killed him; Ali then prayed for the Jinn.
Abdullaah bin Mahmood reports that men of the Khath'am tribe accepted Islaam after a Jinn's call, heard while they stood by their idol, announced the Prophet's Nabuwwaat.
Tameem Daari recounts hearing a Jinn in Shaam announce the Prophet's coming, then consulting a monk who confirmed it, and then accepting Islaam.

Waathila bin Asqa reports that Hajaaj bin Ilaat, frightened in a valley at night, heard a Jinn recite a verse of Surah Rahmaan, then went to the Prophet and accepted Islaam, while Aas bin Waail dismissed the story among the Quraysh.
Ubay bin Ka'b reports that a Jinn who had heard the Prophet guided a group of lost travellers, who were close to death, to water and the road.
Sa'eed bin Shuyaym reports that his father heard an unseen voice in Uyaynah's army warning that their families were under attack, so they all turned back during the Battle of Khaybar.
Abu Hurayrah reports the Prophet's account of seizing a Shaytaan at night and releasing him after recalling the du'aa of Sulaymaan, and Abu Dardaa gives a similar account.
notes: Two reports: Abu Hurayrah's account and Abu Dardaa's variant.

summary: Buraydah reports that Mu'aadh bin Jabal caught a Shaytaan stealing Sadaqah dates, and the Shaytaan taught him Aayatul Kursi and the end of Surah Baqarah.
Abu Hurayrah catches a Shaytaan taking from the zakaah of Ramadhaan, who teaches him Aayatul Kursi, and Abu Ayyoob Ansaari tells of a Jinn stealing his dates.
notes: Abu Hurayrah's account and a separate report from Abu Ayyoob Ansaari.

summary: Cross-reference only: it notes that a similar narration about Ubay bin Ka'b has already been quoted in the chapter on Dhikr.
notes: Editorial cross-reference with no narration in it; themes are taken from the heading and the chapter it points to.

summary: Abu Waa'il reports Ibn Mas'ood's account of a Companion who wrestled a Shaytaan three times and learned a verse of Surah Baqarah from him, and Ibn Mas'ood names that Companion as Umar.
Ibn Mas'ood tells of a Companion who floored a Jinn three times, learned Aayatul Kursi from him, and whom he identifies as Umar.
notes: Variant of the n03578 incident, told in a separate narration.

summary: Mujaahid says the Shaytaans were chained during Umar's khilaafah and were released only after his martyrdom.
Aamir bin Abdullaah reports that Abdullaah bin Zubayr rebuked a Jinn he met at Yanaasib, and that his companions then fell from their animals.
notes: Approved list marks aamir-bin-abdullaah-bin-zubayr as not sahabi, but the text gives (RA). Approved id used; status needs checking.

summary: Abu Sulaymaan Daaraani reports that Abdullaah bin Zubayr, camped at Tabook, lunged at an old man on his animal, who then warned him, and Ibn Zubayr rebuked him in return.

Suwayd bin Zaid reports Abu Dharr's account of pebbles in the Prophet's hands glorifying Allaah in the hands of Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthmaan, and the Prophet said this denotes the successors of Nubuwwah.
notes: Suwayd's report with Abu Dharr's account and a variant ('another narration adds') that is cut off mid-sentence.

summary: Abu Dharr adds that the pebbles also glorified Allaah in Ali's hand, and in the hands of the other Companions they stayed silent.
notes: Two variant reports of the pebbles incident.

summary: Ibn Mas'ood recounts the Prophet's miracles: water gushing from between his fingers, and food glorifying Allaah as it was eaten.
notes: Ends with a cross-reference to the du'aa chapter about Abbaas.

summary: Jaabir reports that the palm trunk the Prophet used to lean on wept like a child when he left it for the new pulpit.
Further reports describe the palm trunk moaning like a camel until the Prophet came back and embraced it, and Hasan used to tell this to remind people of their longing for the Prophet.
notes: Several variant reports (Jaabir's, Anas's, Hasan's, and an extended version). 'Hasan' is matched to hasan-bin-abil-hasan, not checked.

summary: Abul Bakhtari reports that Salmaan and Abu Dardaa saw a plate and the food on it glorify Allaah while they ate, and Qais adds that they often reminded each other of it.
notes: Abul Bakhtari's report and a separate report from Qais.

summary: Ja'far bin Abu Imraan reports that Abdullaah bin Amr heard a fire say it too seeks Allaah's protection from the immense Fire.
notes: Cut off mid-sentence ('...the immense fire (of').

summary: Yahya bin Ayyoob reports that a devoted youth who fell unconscious on remembering Allaah when tempted by a woman later died, and that when Umar recited a verse at his grave, the youth answered that he had been given both gardens of Jannah.
notes: Contains a citation line (Al Bidaayah) naming other Companions. Treated as a reference, not as narrators.

summary: A variant says the youth asked Umar to pass on his greetings and to ask about the reward for fearing standing before one's Rabb, and Umar then told the grave it would have two gardens.
notes: Two variant reports of the n03590 incident.

summary: Muhammad bin Himyar reports that Umar greeted the dead at Baqee Gharqad, and a voice replied that the deeds sent ahead were found and the wealth left behind was lost.
Abdullaah bin Umar reports seeing Abu Jahal in a pit near Badr being punished, which the Prophet confirmed would last until the Day of Qiyaamah.
Sa'eed bin Musayyib reports that Zaid bin Khaarija spoke after death, naming the Prophet and the first three Khalifas and foretelling the trials to come, and that a man of Banu Khatmah did the same.
notes: Two incidents in one report: Zaid bin Khaarija and an unnamed man of Banu Khatmah.

summary: Nu'maan bin Basheer reports that Zaid bin Khaarija spoke from beneath his covering, affirming the Prophet's prophethood and praising Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthmaan, and foretelling trials.
notes: The 'one in the middle' praised as Ameerul Mu'mineen is unnamed here, so not tagged as Umar.

summary: Nu'maan bin Basheer says that while waiting for Uthmaan to lead the prayer, Zaid bin Khaarija raised his shroud, greeted them and spoke, asking about Abdullaah bin Rawaaha and his fathers; a variant adds more of his speech and a verse about Jahannam.
notes: Nu'maan's account plus variants ('another narration' and 'another narration adds'). Cut off mid-sentence at 'May Allaah's peace... be showered on you,'. 'Sa'd' is not identified.

summary: Nu'maan bin Basheer reports Zaid bin Khaarija's corpse speaking about the strength of the Khulafaa, Uthmaan's forgiveness and the coming trials, and greeting the Prophet and Abdullaah bin Rawaaha while asking after his father Khaarija bin Zaid.
notes: Cut off mid-sentence ('The well of Arees has been seized').

summary: Anas bin Maalik recounts how a Muhaajir mother's du'aa over her dead son brought him back to life, and he ate with them; a variant identifies her as Ummu Saa'ib.
notes: Anas's account and a variant that names the woman as Ummu Saa'ib.

summary: Abdullaah bin Aun reports Anas bin Maalik's account that when the Prophet sent him to tell a Muhaajir woman her son had died, her du'aa brought the boy back to life, and he lived until the Prophet died.
notes: The narration says it continues and will be related later on; the rest is in a later section.

summary: Abu Nadhra reports Jaabir bin Abdullaah's account that his father, the first to be martyred at Uhud, asked him to settle his debts and treat his sisters well, and that his body was found unchanged six months later.
notes: Abu Nadhra's report plus two 'another narration' variants. The father is not named in the text.
